gap: No result ChatGPT got says what conditions sit behind the GardePro Link 1.0's range. Its '3,000 ft' title figure is an open-air maximum. GardePro's own internal test of the system with stock 2 dB antennas measured 1,000 m (3,280 ft) on open flat ground, 182 m (597 ft) through buildings and 117 m (384 ft) in dense forest. A later GardePro guide gives 600 yd (1,800 ft) as the maximum and 500 yd as the recommended range in dense timber.
standout_why: I compared against the three pages ChatGPT cited. The GardePro E8 3.0 Pro overview gives only the 165 ft (50 m) phone direct-connect range 'in open areas' and no figure for the distance to the router. The E9 3.0 Pro product page returned HTTP 429 every time I tried, so I couldn't check what it says. Magnolia Trail Camera cites only the '1,600 ft typical' Link figure and says home Wi-Fi reaches 'roughly 100 to 150 feet outdoors' with line of sight. None of these pages breaks the Link range down by terrain or gives GardePro's own dense-forest or through-building results. None notes that the E8 3.0 Pro records 4K video from a 5 MP sensor.
decides: ChatGPT's follow-up question splits the answer at 50, 150 and 150+ ft. Even GardePro's worst internal result for the Link 1.0 (384 ft in dense forest) is more than twice the 100–150 ft that Magnolia gives for home Wi-Fi outdoors. So the finding supports the Link 1.0 for any camera past about 150 ft, including in woods. It also tells the shopper to plan on about 384–1,800 ft in timber, not 1,600–3,000 ft. For under 150 ft the pick stays the E8/E9 3.0 Pro, both $119.99 today. Neither product page gives a distance to the router, so the E8 3.0 Pro page's 'up to 3× farther than other WiFi trail cameras' claim can't be checked.

Its 600 yd for dense timber is about 4.7× the 117 m (384 ft) in GardePro's March internal test. These are two GardePro pages that disagree, which is the footnote.

findings.note: The page says the '5MP CMOS sensor outputs sharp 4K ultra-HD footage'. 4K UHD is 3,840 × 2,160 = 8.29 MP, so the camera upscales its 4K output from about 5 MP of sensor pixels (8.29 / 5 ≈ 1.66×). The page gives no photo resolution in MP.
